metadata.case_name: LAU WA YING v. CARITAS - HONG KONG

plaintiff.occupation_before: personal care worker in elderly homes (PCW)

injuries.description: the diagnosis was a soft tissue injury of back
source: the diagnosis was a soft tissue injury of back
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of muscle, fascia or tendon of lower back

injuries.description: diagnosed with lower back and left foot sprain with soft tissue injury
source: diagnosed with lower back and left foot sprain with soft tissue injury
injuries.icd_description: Strain or sprain of lumbar spine

injuries.description: a number of degenerative changes in her lower back
source: MRI on 27 August 2013 which showed a number of degenerative changes in her lower back
the degenerative changes in the spine should be pre-existing
injuries.icd_description: Injuries to the abdomen, lower back, lumbar spine or pelvis

source: The diagnosis was Major Depressive Disorder, Single Episode, which was caused by the accident and from which the plaintiff has recovered.

manifestations.description: continuous and non-stop low back pain on the left side
numbness of the left lower limb on the lateral aspect of the left thigh, leg and sole with pinpricking or no sensation
intermittent left scapular pain since December 2013
depressed mood, worries, annoyance, poor memory, poor sleep, self-blame, appetite loss and suicidality
visual hallucination with insomnia (attended A&E of PMH complaining of visual hallucination with insomnia)

treatments_received.treatment: A&E attendance and discharge with medication
source: the plaintiff attended the Accident and Emergency Department ("A&E") of Princess Margaret Hospital ("PMH") the next day after the accident at about 2 pm. Physical examination showed mild tenderness over her lower back and the sole of her left foot. X-ray showed no bone fracture. No neurological sign was noted. She was discharged with medication. Two days’ sick leave was given up to 8 August 2013.

treatments_received.treatment: Tung Chung Outpatient Clinic consultation (diagnosed with lower back and left foot sprain with soft tissue injury)
source: On 9 August 2013, she attended Tung Chung Outpatient Clinic and was diagnosed with lower back and left foot sprain with soft tissue injury. Three days’ sick leave was given up to 12th August.

treatments_received.treatment: Consultations with a Chinese medical practitioner (four times)
source: From 13th to 20th August, she consulted a Chinese medical practitioner four times, each time she was given two days’ sick leave.
The plaintiff had an MRI on 27 August 2013 which showed a number of degenerative changes in her lower back.

treatments_received.treatment: Consultations with Dr Clarence Cheung (five visits) and sick leave issued
source: On 28 August 2013, the plaintiff went to see Dr Clarence Cheung and was given eight days’ sick leave back dated to begin from 22 August and ended on 29 August 2013. On 29th August, the next day after she last consulted him, she saw him again and was given sick leave for seven days. In sum, she went to see Dr Cheung five times, each time on the day the last sick leave expired. She obtained sick leave from him up to 8 October 2013.

treatments_received.treatment: Consultations with Dr Pun Kam Wa (nine times) complaining of continuous ache from left side of lower back radiating to left sole
source: Then, from 3 October 2013 to 24 January 2014, she consulted Dr Pun Kam Wa nine times, complaining of continuous ache from left side of her lower back radiating to left sole.

treatments_received.treatment: Admission to Emergency Medicine Ward (PMH) 16 October 2013 to 18 October 2013
source: On 16 October 2013, Dr Pun referred the plaintiff to A&E of PMH upon her expressing low mood and suicidal ideas. The plaintiff was then admitted to Emergency Medicine Ward ("EMW") of PMH up to 18 October 2013 when she was allowed discharge against medical advice.

treatments_received.treatment: Physiotherapy (13 sessions) from North Lantau Hospital from 11 December 2013 up to 5 March 2014
source: In the meantime, the plaintiff received 13 sessions of physiotherapy treatments from North Lantau Hospital ("NLH") since 11 December 2013 up to 5 March 2014. Since 5 March 2014, she defaulted treatment from physiotherapy department of NLH.

treatments_received.treatment: Admission and transfer for psychiatric management: admitted to EMW of PMH on 6 March 2014; transferred to Kwai Chung Hospital from 7 March until 1 April 2014
source: On 6 March 2014, the next day after the expiry of last sick leave, the plaintiff attended A&E of PMH complaining of visual hallucination with insomnia. She was admitted into EMW of PMH. On 7 March 2014, she was transferred to Kwai Chung Hospital for further management of emotional instability and destructive behaviour. She was admitted into Kwai Chung Hospital from 7 March until 1 April 2014.

treatments_received.treatment: Occupational Therapy: work hardening program from North Lantau Hospital from 28 May 2014 to 31 December 2014
source: In the meantime since 28 May 2014, the plaintiff was referred by PMH to Occupational Therapy Department of NLH where she received work hardening program with little progress until 31 December 2014.

treatments_received.treatment: Orthopaedic outpatient follow-up from 19 March 2014 until 20 July 2015
source: On 19 March 2014, she was first seen by the Orthopaedic Outpatient Clinic of PMH and since has been regularly followed-up by it until 20 July 2015.

treatments_future.treatment: psychiatric treatment from private sector for a further period of about three to six months
source: Dr Wong recommended psychiatric treatment from private sector for a further period of about three to six months essentially to counsel her out of the "abnormal sick role".

losses.description: continuous and non-stop low back pain on the left side; numbness of the left lower limb on the lateral aspect of the left thigh, leg and sole with pinpricking or no sensation; intermittent left scapular pain
